stem.en: If all unicellular organisms were grouped into a single kingdom, what problem would arise?

text.en: Plants and animals would have to join that one kingdom too.

feedback.en: Plants and animals are multicellular, so they would stay outside it.

text.en: Multicellular organisms would be left with no kingdom at all.

feedback.en: Multicellular organisms would keep their own kingdoms. The problem lies inside the new one.

text.en: Cells with and without a true nucleus would share one kingdom.

feedback.en: Right. Bacteria have no true nucleus and Amoeba has one, and that is a deep difference in cell type.

text.en: All the organisms in that kingdom would have to make their own food.

feedback.en: Grouping does not change how organisms feed. Amoeba would still depend on others for food.

explanation.en: Bacteria are prokaryotes and Amoeba is a eukaryote. One kingdom for all single cells would hide that difference, which is why Monera and Protista are separate.

hints.en: Think of two single-celled organisms that differ in cell type.
